answer: Sybils are cheap until they must be somewhere. Over weeks, scattered verifiers send staggered pings and each identity builds one consistent latency map, anchored like basalt: light-speed bounds leave it only one narrow region it can honestly claim. A thousand clones behind three relays form a nebula of invented locations, yet every bridge between their claimed homes and their measured delays collapses to those three exits. Faking dispersion then means renting real machines everywhere, per identity, forever.
